claims.explanation: These three pairs are impossible because j must be one of 1,...,9, so they cannot belong to the list of possible outcomes. The corrected list must omit them and include the nine zero-difference pairs (1,1),...,(9,9).
After excluding the three impossible pairs from the list of 15, 15 - 3 = 12. Thus the number of listed nonzero-difference pairs is 12, not 13.

claims.quoted_text: (1,9), (5,9), (9,5), (9,1) \) because these four cases will result in a difference of \( \pm 8 \), which is not a multiple of 4 but rather a multiple of 8
claims.explanation: (5,9) and (9,5) produce differences 4 and -4, not ±8. Moreover, 8 and -8 are themselves multiples of 4, so none of these pairs should be excluded; all differences 4, -4, 8, -8 satisfy the condition.
